function.name: user_mandates
function.description: Fetches the mandates associated with a user based on the provided user name and the status of the mandates. This API is intended for use by partners to retrieve information about their clients' mandates. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

name.description: The full name of the partner's client for whom to fetch mandates.

status.description: The status of the mandates to be fetched. If omitted, mandates of all statuses will be retrieved.

function.name: partner_mandates
function.description: Fetches the mandates associated with a partner based on the specified status. If no status is provided, all mandates are retrieved. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

status.description: The status of the mandates to be fetched. If left empty, mandates with any status will be retrieved.

message.content:
A **mandate** is an official authorization or instruction that gives someone the authority to act on behalf of another party. In many contexts—especially in finance, law, or business—a mandate defines the scope, limits, and responsibilities of the authorized person or entity. For example:

| Context | What the mandate typically covers |
|---------|-----------------------------------|
| **Financial services** | A client authorizes a broker or financial adviser to execute trades, manage investments, or provide advice. |
| **Legal representation** | A lawyer receives a mandate from a client to represent them in court or negotiate contracts. |
| **Corporate governance** | A board member may receive a mandate to oversee certain projects or approve specific decisions. |
| **Government** | An elected official may have a mandate from voters to pursue particular policies. |

Mandates can be **active**, **pending**, or **inactive** depending on whether they are currently in effect, awaiting approval, or have been terminated.
